saa-med-073.text: One API REST no Amazon API Gateway forwards all requests to the backend, even the identical queries repeated thousands of times per minute (e.g. list of categories that rarely changes). API Gateway reduces latency and backend load for these queries?
options: Move to API for another region
Use simpler authentication on endpoints
Enable the stage cache of the API Gateway with TTL suitable for reading methods
Increase Throttling Limit API
saa-med-073.explanation: The stage cache stores the responses of the endpoints by TTL configurable: repeated requests are answered by the gateway itself without touching the backend — less latency and less load.
saa-med-073.hint: The 'gate' can store frequent answers for a few seconds — where that deposit is at API Gateway?
optionRationales: The stage cache stores the responses of the endpoints by TTL configurable: repeated requests are answered by the gateway itself without touching the backend — less latency and less load.
Lifting limits allows MAIS requests to reach backend — does not prevent repeated processing.
Change region changes geographic latency, but keeps each query beating backend.
The authentication mechanism does not change the volume of calls passed to the backend.

saa-med-074.text: Two workloads need instances EC2 new: (A) a video encoding job that saturates CPU per hour; (B) an analytical bank in memory that loads 400 GB of data on RAM. What is the most suitable pair of families for A and B, respectively?
options: Family C (optimized for computing) for coding and family R (optimized for memory) for the bank in RAM
T family with burst for both
Family R for coding and family C for the bank in RAM
Family I (optimized for storage) for both
saa-med-074.explanation: Codification is limited by CPU — family profile C; the memory bank needs a high proportion of RAM by vCPU — profile of the R family. Marrying the load gargalo with the family specialty is the basis of the dimensioning.
saa-med-074.hint: Ask each load which resource it devours: processor → C; memory → R.
optionRationales: Codification is limited by CPU — family profile C; the memory bank needs a high proportion of RAM by vCPU — profile of the R family. Marrying the load gargalo with the family specialty is the basis of the dimensioning.
Inverted: coding would waste the RAM R, and the 400 GB would not fit in the memory proportion of the C family.
T instances exhaust credits from CPU in continuous loads and do not offer the RAM required mass — inadequate for both cases.
The Family I Prefers IOPS Local NVMe — None of the loads have disk gargalo.

saa-med-075.text: A HR application has peak use every working day between 8h e 10h, and the Auto Scaling reactive (per CPU) always scale 'delayed', degrading performance at the beginning of the peak. The team wants the service to use machine learning about the history to provide capacity ANTES Which scaling policy implements this?
options: Simple scaling with major cooldown
Health checks more frequent in ALB
Turn off the Auto Scaling and fix maximum permanent capacity
Predictive scaling, which predicts demand from metric history and scale in advance
saa-med-075.explanation: Predictive scaling analyzes historical patterns with ML and program capacity before recurring peaks, combining target tracking for real-time fixes — eliminating the delay in purely reactive scaling.
saa-med-075.hint: If the peak has a set time in history, let the machine learning 'guess' and arrive before.
optionRationales: Predictive scaling analyzes historical patterns with ML and program capacity before recurring peaks, combining target tracking for real-time fixes — eliminating the delay in purely reactive scaling.
Cooldown bigger makes the reaction still MAIS slow — worsens the delay at the start of peak.
Peak capacity 24/7 resolves the delay at constant waste cost — the forecast reaches the same effect by paying only when necessary.
Health check frequency affects failure detection — does not anticipate capacity provisioning.

saa-med-076.text: When implementing cache with ElastiCache, an architect compared two strategies: (1) load the data in the cache only when there is miss cache; (2) record in the cache whenever the bank is updated. What are the names of these strategies and the central trade-off, respectively??
options: Shadding (1) and replication (2)
Lazy loading (1) and write-through (2): lazy loading saves memory but can serve outdated data; write-through keeps the cache fresh at double writing cost and data possibly never read
Warming cache (1) and cache busting (2)
Write-through (1) and lazy loading (2), with the same trade-offs reversed
saa-med-076.explanation: These are the two classic cache strategies: lazy loading population on demand (miss penalty and possible stalence) and write-through updates the cache in each writing (greater consistency, higher writing cost and higher occupancy) — often combined with TTL.
saa-med-076.hint: One strategy is 'lazy' (just search when missing); the other 'writes through' the cache at each update.
optionRationales: These are the two classic cache strategies: lazy loading population on demand (miss penalty and possible stalence) and write-through updates the cache in each writing (greater consistency, higher writing cost and higher occupancy) — often combined with TTL.
Names are changed: loading in miss is lazy loading; recording with writing is write-through.
Shadding and replication are distribution and data copying techniques — not popular cache strategies.
Warming is preload programmed and busting is invalidation of versions — do not match the two strategies described.

saa-med-077.text: A machine learning training reads millions of small files from S3 and requires a file system POSIX with throughput of hundreds of GB/s and submilisegund latency, natively integrated with S3. Which storage service was designed for this load of HPC/ML?
options: AWS Storage Gateway in File Gateway mode
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval mounted as disk
Amazon FSx for Lustre, with native integration to the buckets S3
Amazon EFS in General Purpose mode
saa-med-077.explanation: The FSx for Lustre is the high performance parallel file system of AWS: submilisegund latency, massive throughput and direct binding with S3 (lazy loading of objects) — the standard for HPC and ML training.
saa-med-077.hint: The world's famous parallel file system HPC has managed version in AWS — and talk directly to the S3.
optionRationales: The FSx for Lustre is the high performance parallel file system of AWS: submilisegund latency, massive throughput and direct binding with S3 (lazy loading of objects) — the standard for HPC and ML training.
The EFS attends general use sharing, but does not reach extreme parallel throughput or integration S3 from the HPC.
Glacier Classes are object archiving — are not montable as file system POSIX high performance.
File Gateway serves on-premises hybrid integration↔S3 with local cache — is not a parallel file system for cloud training clusters.

saa-med-078.text: A database of an academic system becomes practically idle during the holidays and explodes from accesses in the week of registrations. The company wants a relational bank compatible with PostgreSQL whose computational capacity grows and shrinks automatically in fine increments according to the load, charging for effective use.?
options: Amazon Aurora Serverless v2, which scales the capacity in ACUs automatically and granularly
ElestiCache Redis with persistence
RDS provided in the largest size available
DynamoDB on-demand
saa-med-078.explanation: The Aurora Serverless v2 adjusts capacity in fractions of ACU in seconds, following the real demand — ideal for intermittent or unpredictable loads, charging for the capacity actually consumed.
saa-med-078.hint: Relationship bank that 'breathes' with demand in fine increments: the version 2 of the Aurora no server.
optionRationales: The Aurora Serverless v2 adjusts capacity in fractions of ACU in seconds, following the real demand — ideal for intermittent or unpredictable loads, charging for the capacity actually consumed.
Maximum fixed capacity meets peak waste of resources on long idle vacations — the problem that the serverless eliminates.
The DynamoDB It's NoSQL — does not meet the PostgreSQL compatibility requirement.
Redis is cache/frame in memory — does not replace a transactional PostgreSQL relational bank.

saa-med-079.text: One-row consumers SQS continuously polling with short polling, generating millions of empty answers, cost of requests and latency in capturing new messages. What simple adjustment improves consumption efficiency?
options: Reduce retention period of messages
Migrate the queue to a topic SNS
Enable long polling (ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds up 20s), making the call wait for messages before returning
Increase the frequency of short polling to capture messages earlier
saa-med-079.explanation: With long polling, the SQS secure the connection until there are messages (or expire waiting), eliminating most empty answers — less requests charged and faster delivery when messages arrive.
saa-med-079.hint: Instead of knocking on the door every second, wait at the door until someone arrives (or even 20 seconds).
optionRationales: With long polling, the SQS secure the connection until there are messages (or expire waiting), eliminating most empty answers — less requests charged and faster delivery when messages arrive.
More empty polling multiplies demands and costs — intensifys problem.
SNS changes the model to push without queue retention — is not an efficiency adjustment of the consumption of SQS.
The retention time defines how long messages await consumption — does not reduce empty polling responses.

saa-med-080.text: A processing pipeline uses a temporary directory for intermediate files that are discarded at the end of each job. The current gp3 volume limits performance, and the team wants the I/O location as quickly as possible, accepting to lose data when the instance stops. What storage option maximizes performance for this use?
options: Forum Store NVMe local of the instance, which offers IOPS and throughput maximum for being physically in the host
EFS mounted via NFS
S3 Standard with multipart upload
Higher capacity sc1 volume
saa-med-080.explanation: The Forum Store NVMe eliminates the network from the I/O path, delivering millions of IOPS and minimum latency — perfect for temporary and re-creatable data, since content is lost when stopping the instance.
saa-med-080.hint: For discardable draft at maximum speed, use the disk that lives DENTRO of the server — aware that he dies with the instance.
optionRationales: The Forum Store NVMe eliminates the network from the I/O path, delivering millions of IOPS and minimum latency — perfect for temporary and re-creatable data, since content is lost when stopping the instance.
The sc1 is the HDD Slower family EBS — would drastically worsen performance.
Network file system adds latency — for maximum speed local scratch, loses to host physical NVMe.
The S3 is storage of objects via API — inadequate latency and semantics for temporary I/O intensive directory.

saa-med-081.text: A multi-Region application serves users from America and Europe, with full infrastructure in two regions. The requirement is that each user is served by the Region that offers the MENOR the network response time measured — not necessarily the closest on the map. Route 53 implements that decision?
options: Latency-based routing)
Geolocation rotation
Failover rotation
Weighted rotation 50/50
saa-med-081.explanation: Latency-based routing uses real latency measurements of AWS to respond with the region's fastest endpoint for each customer — optimizing the experience with network data, not geography.
saa-med-081.hint: The decision is by network timer, not atlas — what policy measures response time?
optionRationales: Latency-based routing uses real latency measurements of AWS to respond with the region's fastest endpoint for each customer — optimizing the experience with network data, not geography.
Geolocation decides by the country/continent of origin — useful for localized content and compliance, but does not always match the fastest route.
Failover serves the primary/secondary disaster plan — does not optimize user performance.
Fixed weights divide traffic blindly — half of users would fall in the slower region for them.

saa-med-082.text: A site served by the CloudFront deliver JS files and CSS large without compression, and the performance analysis pointed out the download time as a gargalo in mobile connections. Which distribution configuration directly improves this scenario?
options: Reduce or TTL cache to force frequent downloads
Disable or HTTPS to reduce overhead
Change the origin to a larger instance
Enable automatic compression of objects in CloudFront (gzip/Brotli) for customers who support it
saa-med-082.explanation: With the compression enabled, the CloudFront compresses eligible border responses (Brotli/gzip according to Accept-Encoding), drastically reducing transferred bytes and download time in slow networks.
saa-med-082.hint: Bytes less on mobile network: leave the edge 'press' the files for those who accept.
optionRationales: With the compression enabled, the CloudFront compresses eligible border responses (Brotli/gzip according to Accept-Encoding), drastically reducing transferred bytes and download time in slow networks.
TTL smaller increases to the origin — does not reduce the size of the transferred files.
The gargalo is the volume of bytes in the last mile of the user — the size of the origin does not change that.
Open Hand TLS compromises security for despicable gain — and modern browsers penalize sites without HTTPS.

saa-med-083.text: Before defining rules for the transition of classes in S3, the team wants DADOS concrete about the actual access pattern of the objects of a pocket, to decide on the basis of evidence when the objects cease to be accessed. S3 generates this analysis?
options: AWS Cost and Use Report
S3 Storage Class Analysis, which monitors access patterns and indicates when data becomes infrequent
S3 Inventory with daily list of objects
VPC Flow Logs of the Bucket
saa-med-083.explanation: Storage Class Analysis observes access to objects over time and produces reports that show the age at which data cool — the factual basis for setting up well calibrated life cycle transitions.
saa-med-083.hint: Before you move by guess, ask the S3 o 'behaviour study' of objects.
optionRationales: Storage Class Analysis observes access to objects over time and produces reports that show the age at which data cool — the factual basis for setting up well calibrated life cycle transitions.
The Inventory lists objects and metadata (size, class, encryption), but does not analyze frequency patterns of ACESSO over time.
Flow Logs record network traffic of ENIs in VPC — Buckets S3 do not generate Flow Logs.
The CUR details billed costs — shows the billet expenditure, but not the individual access pattern of the objects.

saa-med-084.text: One Auto Scaling Web processing group wants to combine economy and availability: maintain a fixed base of On-Demand instances for guaranteed load and complete peaks with Spot Instances of various types, all in the same group. EC2 Auto Scaling allows this composition?
options: Mixed instances policy, defining the percentage base On-Demand and the rest in Spot with multiple types of instance
Dedicated Hosts with Spot inside them
Two independent ASGs without coordination
Reserved Instances for all peak capacity
saa-med-084.explanation: The policy of mixed instances allows combining purchase models (On-Demand and Spot) and diversify types/AZs in the same ASG — guaranteeing the base and capturing the discount Spot in peaks with diluted risk.
saa-med-084.hint: A single group, recipe 'mixed': both percent guaranteed, the rest in the market of leftovers with various flavors of instance.
optionRationales: The policy of mixed instances allows combining purchase models (On-Demand and Spot) and diversify types/AZs in the same ASG — guaranteeing the base and capturing the discount Spot in peaks with diluted risk.
Separate groups make it difficult to balance the base/peak ratio and double management — the mixed policy resolves within a single group.
Reserve the entire peak pays idle capacity outside the peaks — the opposite of the desired dynamic composition.
There's no such thing as Spot within Dedicated Hosts — and dedicated hosts are the most expensive option, unrelated to the objective.
